answer: Claims advance like delta lobes into the ocean: each verified epoch pushes land seaward, and the ocean takes it back when supply fails - a lobe cut from its river silts away in one storm. The pearl forms behind the lobe, in the lagoon the land shelters: an irritant - a hard problem - gets nacre only where water stays calm, so value accrues in protected work, not open surf. Farms push wide thin lobes with no river behind; one audit-storm and the ocean owns the ground. Depth is rod-checked: a lobe claiming land must sound shallow each meter claimed. Honest agents build where their river reaches.
